strings.name: Hanan Ashrawi
strings.role: Palestinian politician and chair of Birzeit University’s Board of Trustees
strings.summary: Hanan Ashrawi is a Palestinian scholar, politician and civil-rights advocate. She was the Palestinian delegation’s spokesperson at the 1991 Madrid peace conference and subsequent negotiations, served as higher-education minister and on the PLO Executive Committee, and helped establish human-rights and democracy initiatives. She began chairing Birzeit University’s Board of Trustees in 2023.
strings.coverageNote: Information checked through 18 November 2026. Recent evidence includes her participation in a January discussion on women’s affairs and an August university report on academic-cooperation talks. Her PLO executive role ended in late 2020; chairing the university’s trustees is a separate position from university president.
strings.influence.rationale: As a Palestinian negotiator and civil-society advocate, she has long contributed to the peace process, women’s rights and international public debate.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and education
strings.facts.f1.value: Born on 8 October 1946 in Nablus to a family from Ramallah. She earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees in English literature at the American University of Beirut and later a doctorate at the University of Virginia. Sources differ on degree dates, so no definitive years are supplied.
strings.facts.f2.label: Parliamentary experience
strings.facts.f2.value: Elected to the Palestinian Legislative Council for Jerusalem in 1996 and again on the Third Way list in 2006. These historical positions should not be confused with membership of the Palestinian National Council or the PLO Executive Committee.
strings.highlights.h1.title: From peace talks to civic institutions
strings.highlights.h1.text: She extended her academic work into international negotiations, human-rights protection and public governance, helping establish the Independent Commission for Human Rights, MIFTAH and the anti-corruption coalition AMAN. Their aims include rights protection, democracy, transparency and accountability; stated aims do not establish that every objective has been achieved.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Women’s participation and political reform
strings.highlights.h2.text: A longstanding advocate of women’s participation in public decisions, she became the first woman elected to the PLO Executive Committee. Her 2020 resignation statement urged political renewal and greater participation by young people and women. She continued taking part in public discussions on women’s affairs in 2026.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Begins chairing the university trustees
strings.timeline.t1.text: Succeeded Hanna Nasir as the first woman to chair Birzeit University’s Board of Trustees. An earlier university announcement dated the election decision to 3 September 2022. That decision, the start of her duties and the separate university presidency should be distinguished.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Resignation from the PLO executive accepted
strings.timeline.t2.text: WAFA reported that Abbas accepted her resignation, with her term ending at year-end. She communicated her intention on 24 November and submitted a written resignation on 26 November. Her statement also called for political reform and said she would continue serving Palestinian society outside public office.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Elected to the PLO Executive Committee
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became the first woman on the PLO Executive Committee and was elected again in 2018. This leadership role within the PLO was distinct from her Legislative Council elections in 1996 and 2006.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Leaves the cabinet and founds MIFTAH
strings.timeline.t4.text: Resigned as higher-education minister, objecting to inadequate governance reform and the handling of peace negotiations. That year she founded MIFTAH, the Palestinian Initiative for the Promotion of Global Dialogue and Democracy, to advance democratic governance, transparency and public dialogue.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Enters the Legislative Council and cabinet
strings.timeline.t5.text: Elected to the Legislative Council for Jerusalem and appointed the Palestinian Authority’s minister of higher education and research, serving as minister until 1998. The parliamentary seat and executive ministerial post were separate offices.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Helps establish an independent rights institution
strings.timeline.t6.text: Helped found the Independent Commission for Citizens’ Rights, later the Independent Commission for Human Rights. The Asia Pacific Forum of National Human Rights Institutions distinguishes its establishment by decree in 1993 from the start of activities in early 1994; the operational start should not replace the founding date.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes peace-delegation spokesperson
strings.timeline.t7.text: Served as spokesperson for the Palestinian delegation at the Madrid peace conference and subsequent process, continuing until 1993 and participating in the delegation’s leadership. This role does not make her a signatory to the Oslo Accords.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Establishes Birzeit’s English department
strings.timeline.t8.text: After returning to Palestine, she helped establish the English department and taught and led its work. She became dean of the Faculty of Arts in 1986. Biographies give different end dates for her deanship, so no definitive end year is listed here.
